records.name: San Luis Potosi
records.summary: No region-specific incident, enforcement or ordinance evidence was found; the state's place in the national map is ordinary compliance: a 2019 reform of the Civil Registry Law created an administrative legal-gender-recognition procedure, with implementing regulations set by gubernatorial decree.

records.name: Sinaloa
records.summary:
No Sinaloa-specific statutes or provisions are supported by the vetted sources for this map. The national picture governs: by March 2025 an international human-rights organization counted 22 of Mexico's 32 states as having legislated legal gender-recognition procedures, with six state legislatures enacting none; a March 2024 report documents that where no procedure exists, trans people face police stops, denied documents and institutional mistreatment.

Transfeminicide has become a criminal category in some states — the capital imposes up to 70 years — against more than 95% homicide impunity nationally, and reporting finds convictions lag the statutes. For a visitor, Sinaloa's own legal record on this map is thin: expect the country-wide picture rather than verified local protections; general-security caution in the region applies independently of any local rights framework.
